title: Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry
seoTitle: Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Wok heat, holy basil, jasmine rice
subtitle: Wok heat, holy basil, jasmine rice
description: Wok heat, holy basil, jasmine rice. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Prep and dry protein
steps.instruction: Pat protein dry. Mince garlic. Measure sauce ingredients — wok moves fast once heat is on.

steps.title: Sear over high heat
steps.instruction: Heat skillet until just smoking. Sear in batches; shrimp 90 seconds per side, chicken to 165°F. Do not crowd.

steps.title: Finish sauce in pan
steps.instruction: Lower to medium. Add butter, garlic, and sauce; toss 1–2 minutes until glossy. Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry should smell bright, not burnt garlic.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.instruction: Serve from the skillet or transfer to warm trays. Backup: foil at 200°F up to 12 minutes — seafood toughens if held too long.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Wok heat, holy basil, jasmine rice. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
